q: While texting and walking, Maya walks right past a friend who is waving at her and never sees him. This is:
exp: She failed to see something visible because her attention was on her phone.
why: "Change blindness" means: Failing to notice changes in the environment because your attention is directed elsewhere.

"Cocktail party effect" means: The ability to focus auditory attention on a particular voice or sound while filtering out others. In a crowded room, you can focus on the voice of the one person you're talking with.

"Stroop effect" means: Delayed reaction time when you must say the color of a word but not the name of the word. Example from your slides: the word GREEN printed in purple, where you have to say "purple."

q: In a movie, an actor's shirt is red in one shot and blue in the next, but most viewers never notice. This is:
exp: Missing a change because attention is directed elsewhere is change blindness.
why: "Inattentional blindness" means: Failing to see visible objects when your attention is directed elsewhere.
"Pop-out phenomenon" means: Something different popping out to get our attention, like the one laughing face in the cartoon of a crying movie audience on your slides.
"Absolute threshold" means: The weakest amount of a stimulus that a person can detect 50% of the time: the moment when you notice something.

q: In a crowded, noisy cafeteria, Eli is talking with one friend when he suddenly hears his own name from across the room. This is:
exp: Your brain can register your name even amongst background noise.
why: "Change blindness" means: Failing to notice changes in the environment because your attention is directed elsewhere.
"Pop-out phenomenon" means: Something different popping out to get our attention, like the one laughing face in the cartoon of a crying movie audience on your slides.
"Weber's law" means: For an average person to perceive a difference, two stimuli must differ by a constant percentage, not a constant amount.

q: You see the word BLUE printed in red ink and must say the ink color. You answer more slowly than usual. This is:
exp: Stroop effect: delayed reaction time when you must say the color of a word, not the word.
why: "Change blindness" means: Failing to notice changes in the environment because your attention is directed elsewhere.
"Bottom-up processing" means: Sensory receptors throughout the body register information about the external environment and send it up to the brain for processing. This is sensation.
"Difference threshold (just noticeable difference)" means: The minimum amount something needs to change before a person notices the change 50% of the time.

q: Raj can taste one teaspoon of salt dissolved in two gallons of water about half the time. This is a measure of his:
exp: The weakest stimulus detected 50% of the time is the absolute threshold.
why: "Difference threshold (just noticeable difference)" means: The minimum amount something needs to change before a person notices the change 50% of the time.
"Selective attention" means: Focusing your conscious awareness on a particular stimulus and NOT something else.
"Top-down processing" means: Using your knowledge, experience, or context to understand and interpret sensory perceptions. This is perception.

q: When Dana turns her car radio from 5 to 6, she doesn't notice, but from 5 to 10 she does. This shows her:
exp: The smallest change you notice 50% of the time is the difference threshold.
why: "Absolute threshold" means: The weakest amount of a stimulus that a person can detect 50% of the time: the moment when you notice something.
"Inattentional blindness" means: Failing to see visible objects when your attention is directed elsewhere.
"Precognition" means: Perceiving future events.

q: You can easily read "Tihs is a vrey smiple snetecne" even though the letters are scrambled. This is mainly:
exp: You read each word as a whole using what you already know. That's top-down.
why: "Bottom-up processing" means: Sensory receptors throughout the body register information about the external environment and send it up to the brain for processing. This is sensation.
"Absolute threshold" means: The weakest amount of a stimulus that a person can detect 50% of the time: the moment when you notice something.
"Change blindness" means: Failing to notice changes in the environment because your attention is directed elsewhere.

q: A psychic tells police where a missing person's body is buried, though she never saw what happened. This claim is called:
exp: Clairvoyance = perceiving events you didn't witness. There's no scientific basis for it.
why: "Telepathy" means: Mind-to-mind communication.
"Precognition" means: Perceiving future events.
"Selective attention" means: Focusing your conscious awareness on a particular stimulus and NOT something else.
